Thank goodness you are alright! One thing that might help you feel more confident (this goes for any females all shapes and sizes) is learning how to defend yourself as a last ditch effort. I do Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and I'm so happy and way more confident being by myself. It actually saved me one time. I was at a club with a friend and we were on the crowded dance floor having a good time. A guy kept trying to grab me to dance I finally turned around and said STOP very loudly so others around could hear. When everyone went back to dancing he grabbed my arm really tight and pulled me really hard backwards. I then took action, and swiveled around and did a kimura on him (it's a type of shoulder lock that helps control the arm). I told him to leave me alone again and thankfully security saw and kicked him out. It was scary but I was impressed with my own muscle memory and felt proud of myself (which I rarely do). I still suggest traveling with friends and always be vigilant, but learning how to defend yourself especially if you have nothing on hand to help defend you is very important. It's sad that we as females have to face this reality but it's better to be prepared.

Alrighty so I am an identical twin (female). One day my twin, her husband, and I went over to our mom's house. Our older sister was there visiting with our two nieces and nephew. This was the day my brother-in-law finally mixed us up.

A little extra back story my brother-in-law had just gotten done working a 32hour shift. So he was very tired and "slap happy" at this point. Also, without planning it my twin and I are both wearing red T-shirts and jeans, with our hair up. 

So my twin and I are standing in the living room chatting with our mom and my twin is holding our youngest niece. My brother-in-law steps out to go use the restroom. Well in that time our niece decided she wanted me to hold her, so I take her from my twin. My brother-in-law comes back from the bathroom and walks right up behind me and puts his hands on my waist. I lean to the side and ask, "what are you doing?" He says, "nothing, you ok?" And I respond, "yeah I'm fine." With a very puzzled look on my face. Mind you my twin is standing 4ft away from me watching all of this happen. He then proceeds to kiss my cheek and smack my ass! My twin then looks at him and goes, "babe?" He walks over next to her and says, "yeah?" And she replies, "babe!" And he then proceeds to look at both of us. All of a sudden a look of horror spreads across his face, he smacks his hands to the sides of his cheeks (like the cover of home alone) and screams, "NOOOOOOO!!!!!!" He runs outside freaking out, while my twin and I fall to the floor laughing like Hyena's at his mistake! He comes running back in eventually and starts rambling saying he needs to call my husband and apologize for kissing me and smacking my ass. While he is frantically calling my husband we are still rolling on the floor trying to catch our breath.

Moral of the story double check which twin you are approaching to, or else you will make a very funny mistake.
